kit: enformer exact kit v0.2 (kits/v0_2): the two extension objects and how they were built

class_builds.a100_80gb: opt/forward/classes/a100_80gb/ — the same sources built with TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=8.0 (sm_80 cubin; serves compute capability 8.x); its CLASS_PINS.json records the objects

toolchain.nvcc: 13.0.88 (Cuda compilation tools, release 13.0, V13.0.88; Build cuda_13.0.r13.0/compiler.36424714_0)
toolchain.host: python 3.11 + torch 2.13.0+cu130 (CUDA 13.0, cuDNN 9.20) headers, g++, ninja — the release stack (environment/requirements.lock) with the CUDA 13.0 compiler wheels added (nvidia-cuda-nvcc / nvidia-cuda-crt / nvidia-nvvm 13.0.88, nvidia-cuda-cccl 13.0.85; CUDA_HOME = site-packages/nvidia/cu13)
toolchain.builder: torch.utils.cpp_extension.load_inline(cpp_sources=_CPP_SRC, cuda_sources=_CUDA_SRC | enformer_xattn.cu, extra_cuda_cflags=['-O3']) — nvcc defaults otherwise: no --use_fast_math, -ftz=false, -prec-div=true, -prec-sqrt=true; the kernels use explicit __f*_rn intrinsics and libdevice expf

rebuild: on a machine with the release stack, the compiler wheels above and the target GPU: set CUDA_HOME / PATH to site-packages/nvidia/cu13, TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST to the target, import kits.v0_2.enformer_fastkit and call load_inline exactly as fused_ext() does (enformer_xattn.ext() for the attention object); copy the produced .so here and record its sha256 and the source digests in this file (and in the class dir's CLASS_PINS.json for a class build), and its `<sha256>  <file name>` line in the SHA256SUMS beside the object — kits.v0_2.check_files re-hashes each object against that line before anything loads it and refuses by name one that differs. kits.v0_2.attach refuses by name an object that lacks an entry point of FUSED_FUNCTIONS.
